investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC only: plain curl GET (descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser, no JS execution) of the venue's official homepage, which embeds its entire programme as a server-rendered WordPress custom-post-type ('event') list directly in the HTML — no separate programme page or REST endpoint was needed. The page's own JSON-LD block is generic WebSite schema only, not Event schema, inspected and ruled out rather than assumed absent.

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://www.katerclub.de/ (katerblau.de redirects here, HTTP 301 — the venue rebranded from 'Kater Blau' to 'Kater' at some point, confirmed by the site's own <title> 'Kater – Nights, Lights & Bubblegum' and its own footer '© 2026 Kater Club') returned a fully server-rendered '#Program' section: 19+ real upcoming WordPress 'event' post articles, each with its own stable WordPress post id in the article's own HTML id attribute (e.g. id="event-1777"), a day/month date-header, a full start–end date+time text range, title, lineup, and (for ticketed nights) an outbound Resident Advisor link. This directly answers the investigation question at Level 1 for the fields the source actually exposes; no dedicated Event JSON-LD, ICS, WordPress Tribe Events REST API, Fourvenues, or Sanity signature was present. No structural/browser escalation was needed; the one genuine gap found (no year stated) is a source limitation, not something a deeper technical probe would resolve.

venue_reference: Kater Blau, now operating as 'Kater' (club, part of the Holzmarkt 25 artists' collective, Mitte, Berlin)

identity.notes: katerblau.de is independently corroborated as the original Kater Blau venue's own domain by multiple third-party discovery sources (Berlin.de, visitBerlin.de, Yelp — treated only as a discovery lead), and issues a live HTTP 301 redirect to www.katerclub.de. The retained page content itself (its own JSON-LD 'name': 'Kater', its own <title> and footer both self-identifying as 'Kater Club', its own Holzmarkt-associated visual branding) is first-party evidence this is the same venue's current official domain under a shortened brand name, not a lookalike or unrelated site — this rebrand (Kater Blau -> Kater) is recorded honestly rather than silently assumed identical.

site_classification.platform: WordPress (Link: rel="https://api.w.org/" header, wp-content/wp-json paths present) with a custom theme rendering its 'event' custom-post-type entries directly and fully server-rendered inside the homepage's Program section — no dedicated calendar plugin (e.g. Tribe Events) signature was found, and no wp-json/tribe/events endpoint was tested since the plain HTML already exposes the same data server-rendered.

title.value: FOREVER 25 curated by Franca & Mimi Love
title.notes: Each event article's own 'date-title' span text, sampled directly (event id 1777).

start_date.notes: Each event article's own 'date-header' span states day and month directly (e.g. '11.09.'), and the entry-summary additionally states a full start-end range as text ('Fr. 11.09 22:00 — Mo. 14.09 01:00') — but NO year is stated anywhere in or near the Program section (only the page footer's unrelated copyright notice states a year). Per docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md's explicit worked example (plausible-but-unstated year based on today's date is AI_INFERENCE, not a valid PROVEN basis), recorded PARTIAL: day/month/time genuinely proven, year genuinely unresolved from this source alone.

time.notes: Each event's own entry-summary text states a start time directly as part of its start-end range (e.g. '22:00' in 'Fr. 11.09 22:00 — Mo. 14.09 01:00'), floating local time, no UTC offset present in the source.

end.notes: The same entry-summary text directly states an explicit end date+time ('Mo. 14.09 01:00') for the sampled multi-day event — unusually, this source DOES state an explicit end unlike Berghain/Tresor/Renate. Year is unresolved for the same reason as start_date.

venue_location.notes: No per-event room/location breakdown is stated on any sampled event article — all events are implicitly the one Kater venue with no sub-room distinction exposed in this source.

source_record_id.notes: Each event article's own HTML id/class attributes directly state its underlying WordPress post ID (e.g. id="event-1777" class="post-1777 event ...") — WordPress's own internal, database-assigned post identifier, a platform-documented stable numeric ID scheme (not an invented hash), matching the policy's 'derived from a deterministic source property whose own stability is itself evidenced' rule. No repeated-fetch empirical stability test was performed in this bounded investigation (a genuine limitation, noted honestly), and there is no public permalink URL exposing this ID directly (see event_url below) — but the ID itself is directly, repeatedly present in the retained markup.

event_url.notes: No dedicated per-event detail page URL is exposed anywhere — events render inline inside the homepage's accordion only; the only outbound per-event link (where present) goes to a third-party ticketing platform (Resident Advisor), not to a first-party event page on this domain.

price.notes: No price figure appears on any sampled event; ticketed nights only link out to Resident Advisor, free ones ('Katergarten') are explicitly described as free entry in their own text.

blockers.description: No year is stated anywhere in or near the Program section, so a real collector cannot honestly resolve start_date/end to a full calendar date from this source alone (same limitation as wilde-renate-berlin-01).

reasons: Identity PROVEN from the venue's own retained page content, corroborated by independent third-party discovery leads, with the Kater Blau -> Kater rebrand recorded honestly rather than silently assumed.

A CONFIRMED public data path retained (19+ real upcoming WordPress 'event' post articles sampled from the live homepage).

title PROVEN with basis DIRECT_SOURCE; start_date honestly assessed as PARTIAL (day/month/time proven, year genuinely unresolved by the source, same limitation as wilde-renate-berlin-01) rather than left blank or guessed.

source_record_id PROVEN via WordPress's own internal, platform-documented post-ID scheme, directly present in the retained markup — stronger identity grounding than wilde-renate-berlin-01, which had no first-party identifier at all.

No unresolved CRITICAL blocker (one MAJOR blocker honestly documented: the unresolved year).

Reaching only READY_FOR_OFFLINE_PROOF, not READY_FOR_ACTIVATION: beyond the missing DETERMINISTIC_DERIVATION offline-proof step (separate follow-up work per this task's own scope), the year-ambiguity is a genuine open design question a collector build would need to resolve (e.g. cross-referencing the RA ticket link, out of scope here) before activation would be appropriate.
